method: Manual reading of all eight raw V5.1 responses with typed evidence, forecast records and equations; single unblinded review

items.finding: All prompts retain the three fixed local relations and the archived parameter-specific refutation; both retention decisions reproduce computed compatibility. These relation objects were supplied by the workflow, not newly invented by Luna.

Both assessments cite the correct model and precommitted parameter version; threshold judgments agree with observed errors. All six status updates are weakened. Neither assessment substitutes refitted CV for prospective error.
Both revise proposals duplicate existing b4_r0 equations and parameter bounds. Initial-value differences do not create a new structure. Graph merges both; zero new structures were fitted.

First proposal calls the extra trace faster, but it has no enforced parameter ordering or established physical interpretation. Treat as an unverified motivation, not a demonstrated timescale mechanism.
Both boundaries abstain. Rich time-condition grammar was available but unused; no new boundary was discovered or validated.

Luna chose families, targets and ranges. The finite numerical compiler chose exact inputs using predicted contrast and novelty. First pair exceeded separation guard; second tested local mirror extension.

Final selected_id v3_r2 and generated explanation agree because the frozen numerical rule produces both; this does not demonstrate autonomous final choice by Luna. Weakened candidates remain eligible by design.

Final b4_r0 has five of 37 CV fits without an optimizer convergence flag. v3_r1 and v3_r2 converge in all 37 folds under the finite budget. Infer comparative prediction performance under this budget, not physical falsification of all parameterizations.

V5.1 had identical initial numerical models to V5 but different initial model proposals. Runs are not a controlled causal estimate of the wording fix. Final eight-input comparison uses one previously inspected system.
